name: Shuah
overview: Shuah is a male figure in Scripture identified as a son of Abraham through his wife Keturah. Beyond this lineage, no further tribal affiliation or additional notes are recorded. His mention is brief and centers on his genealogical position.
namesAndTitles: The name Shuah is a proper name meaning 'depression' or 'lowland' in Hebrew. This name was not given directly by God but is recorded in Genesis 25:2. No titles or additional names are associated with him in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shuah as a son of Abram (Abraham) and Keturah, indicating his place among Abraham's descendants. No other family relationships or descendants are noted beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Shuah's significance lies primarily in his role within the genealogical record of Abraham's descendants after Sarah's death, as recorded in Genesis 25:2. He represents part of the expansion of Abraham's lineage through Keturah, underscoring God's faithfulness in multiplying Abraham's offspring. Though not central to the primary covenant line through Isaac, Shuah contributes to the broader narrative of God's blessings upon Abraham's family.
